rows.q: How much is a routine cleaning?
rows.answer: Routine recall exam: $65. Standard cleaning (scale and polish, about 30 minutes): $120. Routine cleanings are often booked two to three weeks ahead.

rows.q: What does a root canal on a molar cost?
rows.answer: Root canal treatment is priced by tooth position:. Molar: $1,290. A crown is usually needed after a root canal on a molar.

rows.q: What is the price of in-office teeth whitening?
rows.answer: In-office whitening (one visit, about 90 minutes): $480. Take-home whitening trays with gel: $320. Whitening is not recommended while you have untreated cavities or gum disease.

rows.q: How much is a custom night guard?
rows.answer: Custom night guard for teeth grinding: $450.

rows.q: Do you direct bill my insurance company?
rows.answer: We direct bill most major Canadian group insurance plans. Please bring your insurance card to every appointment, and tell us if your plan changes. If we cannot direct bill your insurer, we give you a detailed receipt and you can submit the claim yourself.

rows.q: Which payment methods do you accept?
rows.answer: We accept Visa, Mastercard, debit cards and Interac e-Transfer. We do not accept cheques or cash payments over $500.

rows.q: Can I pay for a big treatment in instalments?
rows.answer: For treatment over $500 you can split the cost into three equal monthly instalments with no interest, through Maple Pay. The first instalment is charged on the day of treatment.

rows.q: How long does insurance pre-approval take?
rows.answer: I don't know the answer to that from our documents. I have passed this conversation to our team. Someone will follow up during opening hours.

rows.q: How much notice do I need to give to cancel an appointment?
rows.answer: Please give us at least 24 hours notice if you need to cancel or reschedule. Notice makes the time available for someone who is waiting in pain. Cancelling with less than 24 hours notice, or missing an appointment: $60 for appointments up to 60 minutes.

rows.q: What is the fee if I miss my appointment?
rows.answer: Cancelling with less than 24 hours notice, or missing an appointment: $60 for appointments up to 60 minutes. The same, for appointments longer than 60 minutes: $100. The fee is not covered by insurance.

rows.q: When do I get appointment reminders?
rows.answer: We send a text message reminder 48 hours before your appointment and another 24 hours before it. Reply STOP to turn text reminders off. We use your information to provide dental care, to bill you and your insurer, and to send appointment reminders.

rows.q: What happens if I arrive late to my appointment?
rows.answer: Cancelling with less than 24 hours notice, or missing an appointment: $60 for appointments up to 60 minutes. The same, for appointments longer than 60 minutes: $100. We waive the fee the first time it happens.

rows.q: How long is the first visit for a new patient?
rows.answer: Please complete the new patient forms online at least 24 hours before your visit.

rows.q: What should I bring to my first appointment?
rows.answer: Please bring your insurance card to every appointment, and tell us if your plan changes. Bring your approval letter or your card on your first visit so we can check what is covered.

rows.q: Are you taking new patients?
rows.answer: Both clinics are accepting new adult patients and families. We see patients of all ages. Comprehensive new patient exam with x-rays: $145.

rows.q: Which languages does your team speak?
rows.answer: Our team speaks English, French, Gujarati, Hindi and Mandarin. Ask us if you would like an interpreter for another language and we will try to arrange one. We do not store the content of chat conversations unless you ask to speak to a team member.

rows.q: Where can I park at the Danforth clinic?
rows.answer: Free parking is available behind the building, with entrance from Birch Alley. The clinic is a five minute walk from the subway and is served by two bus routes. Street parking is available on Example Street, and there are six spaces in the plaza lot.

rows.q: What should I do if my tooth gets knocked out?
rows.answer: Pick the tooth up by the crown (the white part), not the root. A tooth has the best chance of being saved if it is treated within one hour.

rows.q: When should I go to the emergency room instead of the dentist?
rows.answer: Go to the nearest hospital emergency room, or call 911, if you have:. If you are in severe pain at night and cannot wait, go to an emergency room.

rows.q: What is your after-hours emergency phone number?
rows.answer: Outside clinic hours, call (416) 555-0199 and leave a message with your name and number. The line is checked every two hours until 10 pm. We collect your name, address, phone number, email, date of birth, health history, insurance details, and the records of your care.

rows.q: How long should I avoid straws after a tooth extraction?
rows.answer: Bite on the gauze for 30 to 45 minutes after you leave. Do not use a straw, spit, or smoke for 48 hours. Start gentle salt water rinses after 24 hours.

rows.q: When can I chew after getting a filling?
rows.answer: Do not chew until the numbness has gone, so you do not bite your cheek or tongue. Call us if your bite feels high or uneven after the numbness has gone. Avoid chewing on that side until the permanent crown or filling is placed, usually within three weeks.

rows.q: What can I eat and drink after whitening?
rows.answer: For the first 48 hours, avoid coffee, tea, red wine, tomato sauce and other dark foods and drinks.

rows.q: What are your hours on Saturday?
rows.answer: Saturday and Sunday: Closed. Saturday - 9:00 am to 2:00 pm.

rows.q: What is the address of the Lakeshore clinic?
rows.answer: Monday to Friday: 9:00 am to 5:00 pm.

rows.q: Are you open on statutory holidays?
rows.answer: Both clinics are closed on statutory holidays, including New Year's Day, Family Day, Good Friday, Victoria Day, Canada Day, the Civic Holiday, Labour Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas Day and Boxing Day. If your appointment falls on a holiday we will call you to reschedule.

rows.q: How long do you keep my records?
rows.answer: Adult records are kept for 10 years after your last visit. Records for children are kept until 10 years after the child's 18th birthday.

rows.q: Do you sell my personal information?
rows.answer: We share information only with your insurer when we direct bill, with a specialist when you are referred, and with another clinic when you ask us to transfer your records. We do not sell your information to anyone, and we do not share it with advertisers.

rows.q: When should my child first see a dentist?
rows.answer: We recommend a first dental visit by a child's first birthday, or within six months after the first tooth appears. The first visit is short and relaxed.

rows.q: How much is an exam and cleaning for a child under 12?
rows.answer: Exam and cleaning: $95. Patients aged 12 to 17 are charged the adult prices on the Services and Prices page, except for the custom mouthguard.
